description: What a wedding, newborn, family or other event shoot is photographed as. Each scene is a set of plain-English prompts the image model compares a photo against; the studio's words are the labels. A scene is a description, never a verdict: an intentional close-up of a baby's feet and an accidental frame of the floor can look alike, so the engine only calls a frame accidental when it is also technically poor. Changing a prompt means re-running backend/scripts/build-scene-assets.py. Version 2 (measured on the real shoots in the test project against hand labels: 71% of photos labelled right, from 48% with version 1) adds bride and groom portraits, family, friends & guests and emotional moments, names the stage as the reception stage, tightens the ceremony prompts and adds newborn close-ups to details.

calibration.method: Top scene at the confidence culling treats as sure (0.4), on 154 real photos of the test project (100 wedding, 54 newborn) labelled by hand. A scene is validated when it made at least 5 sure calls there and at least 80% were right. Only a validated scene counts toward decisions (a Target Count guarantee, the coverage line, a learned taste); every other scene is still shown as the AI's guess and can be filtered on. Re-measure on more shoots before validating another.
